chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan ibn Bint Iliyas, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May God curse whoever causes an affliction (or sheds blood) or gives shelter to one who has caused an affliction.' I asked: 'What is the affliction?' He replied: 'Killing.'

key_terms.آوَى مُحْدِثًا: gave shelter to the one who caused the affliction

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'hadath' mean in the context of this hadith from Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the term 'hadath' in the Prophet's curse as specifically referring to homicide, thereby narrowing the scope of this severe divine punishment to the act of killing. This narration underscores the gravity of bloodshed in Shia jurisprudence, linking the physical act of murder with the social responsibility of sheltering the perpetrator, a concept rooted in the broader Islamic principle of preserving life.
